Revolution and Republic (1789–1870s)
The French Revolution transformed Paris into a political battleground. The storming of the Bastille in 1789 launched
the revolution. Paris became the seat of radical change: the monarchy fell, the republic rose. Napoleon later
controlled Paris and reshaped it. After his defeat, the city rebuilt and modernized. Urban reform under Napoleon III
in the 1860s created wide boulevards and new infrastructure.
Modern Era (20th century–present)
Paris survived two world wars and emerged as a cultural and political leader. The city modernized with new
transportation systems and housing. Paris joined the European Union framework. Today, it remains a center of fashion,
art, cuisine, and diplomacy. The city blends medieval streets with modern architecture. Paris attracts millions of
visitors annually and maintains its role as France's political and cultural heart.
